frontier_question: Why did Google acquire cloud-security firm Wiz in March 2025, and what did the deal signal about the cloud-security market?

chunks.content: Google announced on 2025-03-18 that it had agreed to acquire Wiz, the cloud-security firm, for approximately $32 billion in an all-cash deal — the largest acquisition in Google's history. The deal followed Wiz's rejection of Google's earlier $23 billion offer in July 2024. Wiz co-founder and CEO Assaf Rappaport remained a named principal in the transaction. Google Cloud, under Thomas Kurian, pursued Wiz to close the security gap with AWS and Azure, betting on cloud-security consolidation as the cloud wars' next battleground and on AI-driven cloud adoption as the demand driver. The deal closed in 2025 after shareholder and regulatory steps, with completion reported in July 2025.

prior_gap_texts: Google acquired the cloud-security firm Wiz to close a security gap with competitors AWS and Azure, betting that cloud-security consolidation would be the next battleground in the "cloud wars" driven by AI-driven cloud adoption [Source: ev-1].
The deal signaled this strategic shift toward securing the market as it consolidated around these new drivers.
The acquisition was announced on March 18, 2025, for approximately $32 billion in an all-cash transaction, making it the largest acquisition in Google's history [Source: ev-1].
This final price followed Wiz’s rejection of an earlier offer from Google worth $23 billion in July 2024 [Source: ev-1].
Although the agreement was reached in March 2025 and involved shareholder and regulatory steps, the deal officially closed later that same year, with completion reported in July 2025 [Source: ev-1].
